cells.tense: The pen is in your hand now, and what arrives next doesn't need to be known in advance.
cells.ask: When something moves you today, name it plainly before you decide anything about it, and leave one thing about it open until tomorrow.
cells.core:
What comes toward you meets someone who can stay with it. Feeling settles in you at its own pace, and you haven't turned that quiet into a decision — you can sit close to something unnamed, and that's what lets it arrive whole instead of split into whatever it's useful for.

So today, keep the naming yours and keep it a step ahead of the closing. Say you'll decide by Friday and watch whether the weight eases or pulls; if it pulls, the deadline came from somewhere other than the thing itself, and dropping it leaves you nearer to what's coming without needing to already be sure.

cells.verb: Letting feeling settle into its own depth before it chooses
cells.place: The turning point where what's coming in meets you

cells.tense: You're standing in a month that hasn't arrived, braced for something still being written ahead of time.
cells.ask: Let one thing you're counting on arrive on its own today — say nothing to it and ask nothing of it until it actually lands.
cells.core:
Feeling what comes in ought to be enough on its own. Instead it gets weighed the moment it shows — who it will matter to, what it will become — and that weighing keeps you out in front of it, past the part you can't plan. When it's going well here, you're by the door as things arrive, not down the hall getting ready for them.

That readiness probably protects something worth protecting, which is what makes it hard to put down. Let one thing unfold with no hand on it, and what you get is the moment it's actually yours, not the version you already managed. If nothing shifts, you've lost a rehearsal.

cells.tense: You're still at a doorway you've already walked through, checking what it wanted from you.
cells.ask: Write down what you notice today before you work out what any of it means, and read the page again tomorrow.
cells.core:
Feeling came in without an owner, so it moved through without taking hold — told later, not lived — and now what shows up gets kept where it can't touch much. When this is working, impressions come in and stay long enough to be told apart, and you can hold one without filing it yet.

Going without the flatness may not be nothing, which is the hard part. Sorting your own impressions from the ones that carry weight, before you work out what they add up to, hands back the whole picture rather than the report of it you've been reading from.

cells.tense: The pen is down while your hand is already moving over something that came in.
cells.ask: Say 'this is settling in me' about one thing you've been calling this week's just what it is.
cells.core:
Feeling in you has been deepening quietly, holding more than it should be able to — and the mood, the season, the people around have been given the credit. When this is acknowledged, the depth is felt as yours while it's still open, before anything asks it to choose; that's what makes it possible to stay in a moment instead of reporting on it later.

Harder than it sounds, because owning it means it could be asked to choose. Noticing hands back closeness that doesn't have to become anything yet — the depth was there before you named it, and it will recognize you when you do.

The asks survive being wrong: they're acts done at a table, useful even if the read is off. Watching for the other rules' traps: no first person, no departed card names, no 'capacity', no wound, and the close of each core in fresh words.
